shortDescription: Zambia's central bank said on Thursday that the government would start issuing 20-year bonds, the longest maturity yet.

children: Zambia's central bank said on Thursday that the government would start issuing 20-year bonds, the longest maturity yet.

The new bond is "aimed at facilitating the development and growth of longer-dated financial instruments in the market," the central bank said as it released its calendar of auctions for the fourth quarter.
The calendar gave Friday, November 20, as the next bond auction date.
Up to now the government has been issuing bonds with maturities of 2, 3, 5, 7, 10 and 15 years.
An International Monetary Fund mission is currently visiting the country for talks on a new support programme.
Zambia is targeting average economic growth of 7% over the next three years as it emerges from protracted negotiations to restructure its external debt.
